Two years ago, Sonos made the leap from wireless speakers into the over-ear headphones market. From the sound of it, Sonos appears to be preparing a higher-end new release with added artificial intelligence features.

Sonos Ace Ultra headphones are about to debut

Chris Welch reports for Bloomberg that Sonos is developing the Sonos Ace Ultra, positioned as a high-end successor to the 2024 Ace headphones.

A U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) filing surfaced on Monday mentioning the product by name, and showing as many as five colour options — a richer palette than the original model's black and white only.

Sonos plans to hold a product launch event in September, and the timing of the filing suggests the Ace Ultra could be one of the stars of that day's event.

The filing also contains technical clues, indicating that the new headphones may support voice command functionality.

Bloomberg reports that CEO Tom Conrad has acknowledged that the original headphones launched without sufficient whole-home integration features, and failed to break through in a fiercely competitive market.

This time, Slos appears intent on tying the hardware more directly to the company's artificial intelligence ambitions.

Conrad has described the company's opportunity as conversational computing and predictive intelligence in the home environment, with Sonos devices serving as the hardware, operating across different rooms and understanding the household's habits.

The company has already extended Sonos Voice Control to support Philips Hue and Lutron Caseta smart home controls.

Meanwhile, Apple's upgraded AirPods Max 2 debuted in March, equipped with the H2 chip, stronger noise cancellation and live translation. Siri artificial intelligence features will also extend to AirPods via iOS 27.

For more information on the upcoming Sonos Ace Ultra headphones, read the full Bloomberg report.
